sub_answers.sub_question: Were there documented disputes or controversies related to hosting, bidding, or government involvement in the 2016 tournament?
What criticisms or official complaints were made regarding match officiating, eligibility, or competitive integrity during the 2016 event?
Were there reported logistical failures, cost overruns, or delays that drew public or media scrutiny during or after the tournament?
What limitations or shortcomings in the tournament's legacy delivery, sustainability, or impact evaluation were identified in post-event reports?
What changes in youth and women's football participation rates in Papua New Guinea and Oceania were recorded after the 2016 tournament?
What legacy projects, infrastructure uses, or development programs were established in Papua New Guinea following the 2016 event?
How did the tournament affect coaching, refereeing, and administrative capacity-building programs in the Oceania region?
What documented economic, tourism, or community development outcomes in Papua New Guinea are attributed to hosting the 2016 tournament?
What were the dates, host cities, and venues for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea?
Which national teams qualified for and participated in the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup?
Which team won the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup and what were the final match score and medalists?
What were the official attendance figures, television coverage, and reported economic figures for the 2016 tournament?
What stadiums, training facilities, and upgrades were used or constructed for the 2016 U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea?
What transport, accommodation, and accreditation systems were implemented for teams, officials, and fans during the tournament?
What roles did FIFA, the Papua New Guinea Football Association, and the local government play in operational planning and delivery?
What security, medical, and matchday operational procedures were documented for the 2016 tournament?

What formal allegations, investigations, legal actions, parliamentary or government inquiries, or audit findings were recorded about the bidding process, host selection, state involvement, public guarantees, or procurement for the 2016 tournament?

Which specific protests, appeals, referee reports, disciplinary cases, tribunal rulings, or official complaints were filed regarding match officiating, player eligibility, eligibility documentation, sanctions, or perceived breaches of competitive integrity during the 2016 event, and what were their outcomes?

What documented project management issues — including missed construction or venue delivery deadlines, contractor disputes, transport or security failures, unplanned emergency expenditures, or audit reports showing cost overruns or unexplained budget variances — were reported during or after the 2016 tournament?

Which post-event evaluations, government or independent audits, academic studies, or NGO reports identified shortfalls in promised legacy projects, sustainability commitments, environmental mitigation, community benefits, or published monitoring and impact-evaluation data for the 2016 tournament, and what specific metrics or projects were cited as incomplete or ineffective?

What measurable changes occurred in girls’ and youth football participation across Papua New Guinea and other Oceania nations after the 2016 tournament (e.g., registered players by age/gender, grassroots program enrollment, school and club uptake, with year-by-year figures or percentage changes)?

Which post-2016 legacy projects and facility uses were implemented in Papua New Guinea (e.g., new or upgraded stadiums, artificial pitches, community football hubs, youth academies or school sport programmes), who funded or managed them, and what are the documented ongoing usage or maintenance plans?

What evidence exists that the 2016 tournament led to expanded coaching, refereeing and football administration capacity in Oceania (e.g., number of OFC/FIFA coaching and refereeing courses delivered, coaching licenses issued, referee accreditation increases, staffing or governance reforms at national associations, with dates and locations)?

Which evaluated economic, tourism or community development impacts in Papua New Guinea have been directly linked to hosting the 2016 tournament (e.g., visitor arrivals, hotel occupancy rates, event-related revenue, temporary or permanent jobs created, community outreach or social programmes, citing official reports or post-event assessments)?

Provide the precise schedule and locations for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea: opening and closing match dates, each host city, and the name and capacity of every stadium used.

List all national teams that secured qualification and actually competed in the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup, including their confederation (e.g., UEFA, CONCACAF) and how each team qualified (e.g., tournament placement, host nation).
Identify the tournament champion of the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup, the final match scoreline and opponent, and the teams awarded silver and bronze (third-place) positions.

Summarize the tournament’s documented spectator and media impact: official total and per-match attendance figures, broadcasters or networks that held TV rights and major viewership numbers if available, and any published economic or tourism impact estimates for Papua New Guinea related to the event.

Which specific stadiums and dedicated training facilities were used for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Papua New Guinea, and what construction or renovation works (including timelines, contractors, capacities, pitch and lighting upgrades, seating additions and funding sources) were completed or commissioned to meet tournament standards?

What transport and accommodation arrangements were put in place for the tournament—including airport arrival procedures, dedicated team coach fleets and shuttle schedules, public transit alterations, the hotels allocated to each national team with room counts and star ratings, and the accreditation system (credential types, access zones, issuance centres, biometric or electronic systems and rollout dates) used for teams, officials and spectators?

How were operational responsibilities divided among key organizations: what formal agreements, memoranda of understanding or contracts specified the roles, funding commitments and oversight tasks of FIFA, the Papua New Guinea Football Association (PNGFA), the national and provincial governments, and the Local Organising Committee in planning and delivering venue management, logistics, staffing and legacy programs?

What documented security, medical and matchday operational procedures were implemented for the 2016 tournament—specifically crowd management and policing plans, stewarding and entry/turnstile protocols, emergency evacuation and incident response plans, on-site medical cover (ambulances, treatment rooms, concussion/trauma protocols), referee and match commissioner operations, and any after-action or incident reports?

What documented disputes, legal challenges, allegations of corruption, or government interventions arose around the bidding, award, or hosting arrangements for the 2016 tournament (e.g., formal protests, court cases, procurement reviews, or resignations by organizing committee officials)?

Which formal complaints, referee or umpire controversies, eligibility disputes, match protests, appeals to governing bodies, or disciplinary rulings were filed concerning officiating, player eligibility, or competitive integrity during the 2016 event (including cases of ineligible players, referee replacement, or overturned results)?

What specific logistical failures, venue or transport breakdowns, contractor delays, construction schedule slips, budget overruns, or emergency incidents were reported during or immediately after the 2016 tournament, and how did media outlets, auditors, or watchdogs quantify the cost or delay impacts?

Which post-event audits, independent evaluations, government or NGO reports identified shortfalls in the tournament’s promised legacy outcomes—such as unused or underfunded facilities, abandoned community programs, missed sustainability targets, or lack of measurable social/economic impact—and what metrics or follow-up plans were cited?

By how much did female and youth participation in organized football (registration numbers, league entries, school programs) change in Papua New Guinea and across Oceania in the 1–5 years after the 2016 tournament, according to PNGFA, OFC reports, national sports ministries, or school-sports enrollment data?

Which specific legacy projects, new or upgraded facilities, permanent community football programs, women’s leagues, coaching academies, or partnerships (for example FIFA Forward or OFC grants) were launched or repurposed in Papua New Guinea as a direct result of hosting the 2016 tournament, and what are their locations and dates of establishment?

What measurable effects on technical capacity in the Oceania football ecosystem—such as numbers of coaching courses run, coaches and referees certified, administration workshops delivered, and subsequent appointments or retention rates—are documented by OFC, national FAs, FIFA, or regional training providers following the 2016 event?

Which published economic, tourism and community-impact indicators (e.g., international visitor numbers, hotel occupancy rates, event-related revenue, temporary and sustained employment, venue utilization rates, or community outreach outcomes) in Papua New Guinea have been attributed to hosting the 2016 tournament in government reports, independent impact studies, tourism authorities, or media analyses?

Provide the tournament dates (opening match through final), the Papua New Guinea host cities and each match venue used for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, including stadium names and their seating capacities during the event.

List every national team that qualified for and took part in the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, giving each country name, its FIFA trigramme, and the confederation (e.g., UEFA, CONCACAF, OFC) by which it qualified.

Identify the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup champion and runner-up, plus the third- and fourth-placed teams; give the final match score, the score of the third-place match, and which countries received gold, silver and bronze.

Report the tournament’s official attendance statistics (total attendance and average per match or per venue), the major television/broadcast rights holders or networks that carried the 2016 U-20 Women’s World Cup (by country or region) and any published viewership figures, and any reported economic data such as tournament revenue, local government spending, or economic impact assessments for Papua New Guinea.

Which stadiums and training venues were used for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea, and what new construction or upgrades (including costs, contractors, timelines, seating capacities, lighting/pitch standards and FIFA certification) were carried out at each facility prior to the tournament?

What transport, accommodation and accreditation arrangements supported teams, match officials and spectators at the 2016 tournament — for example appointed team hotels, official training venue allocations, airport transfer/shuttle schedules and routes, spectator transit plans, accreditation card types, issuance locations and access zones?

How were responsibilities divided among FIFA, the Papua New Guinea Football Association (PNGFA) and Papua New Guinea government bodies for tournament planning and delivery — including the structure and membership of the Local Organising Committee, memorandum of understanding details, funding commitments, procurement oversight and day-to-day operational roles?

What documented security, medical and matchday operational procedures were in place for the 2016 U-20 Women's World Cup in PNG — for example event security plans, policing and crowd-control deployments, emergency/medical response protocols, doping control arrangements, stadium stewarding, volunteer duties and matchday operational checklists?
